subject: Clarifying 'retainless' workflow and audit evidence request
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@medintegra.com>, Paul Turner <paul.turner@medintegra.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifying 'retainless' workflow and audit evidence request

Hi Emma / Paul — thanks for the demo earlier. Quick recap + next steps so we have alignment on the privacy/retention constraints and what Redwood will surface to your security/legal teams.

Call recap (short):
- Goal: MedIntegRA requires no persistent user-identifiable model input storage for PHI workflows; you still need the ability to troubleshoot model failures and run post‑incident analysis.
- Preference: primary model traffic handled in a "retainless" mode (no long-term token storage), with a short-lived KV/debug buffer for transient debugging.
- Concern: auditability & evidence for infosec + legal (SOC2 mapping, dataflow diagram, proof of redaction/pseudonymization).

What Redwood can propose (high-level):
- Retainless-EPH configuration: default 0‑retention for raw inputs; automatic redaction + pseudonymization at ingress for any recognized PHI entities.
- Short-term KV window: opt-in 72‑hour KV cache for debugging, accessible only to MedIntegRA-controlled debug roles and logged with immutable audit records.
- Sampled debug logs: when enabled, token-level traces are sampled and stored separately under a named debug bucket with automatic purge and encryption-at-rest.

Requested artifacts we can provide for your security team:
1) Dataflow diagram showing ingress, redaction, KV window, and audit log flows (attached: medintegra-dataflow-diagram.png).
2) SOC2 control mapping for retention/logging (we will share the mapping doc).
3) Short checklist describing how pseudonymization works in the pipeline (we’ll surface deterministic pseudonymization vs. hashing approach).
4) Redlined pilot proposal (attached: redwood-retainless-proposal.pdf).

Asks / next steps:
- Emma/Paul: please confirm MUST-HAVE constraints (is 0 retention for raw inputs absolute, or is a short KV window acceptable under strict audit?).
- I’ll loop in Rishi for a technical security call (Rishi, are you available Wed/Thu next week?).
- If acceptable, we’ll prepare a 30‑day pilot scope with the Retainless-EPH config + 72‑hour debug fallback and provide a proposed SLA for the pilot.

Thanks — I’ll stand by for confirmation on the MUST-HAVES and a preferred time for a security call.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-retainless-proposal.pdf (application/pdf), medintegra-dataflow-diagram.png (image/png)

Subject: Re: Clarifying 'retainless' workflow and audit evidence request

Thanks, Irene — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying points from our side: 

1) Zero retention for raw inputs: legal is pushing for "no persistent storage of raw PHI-containing inputs." However, our engineering team is worried about not being able to debug production issues. If you are proposing a 72‑hour KV cache that is strictly scoped, sampled, and auditable as you describe, that might be acceptable. Need to see the exact access controls and purge guarantees.

2) Redaction at ingress: can you confirm whether redaction is deterministic (same input => same pseudonym) or one‑way irreversible tokenization? We need deterministic pseudonymization for session re-association in some flows.

3) Timeline for evidence: legal wants the SOC2 control mapping + the dataflow diagram and an example data processing addendum (DPA) clause by the end of next week if possible. Can you also include a short blurb on key rotation & KMS controls?

We appreciate the pilot suggestion. If you can send a redlined pilot that includes the access controls for debug logs and a sample DPA paragraph, we can take this to legal next week.

—Emma
Emma Li
VP Product 
MedIntegRA

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@medintegra.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarifying 'retainless' workflow and audit evidence request

Hi Emma — quick technical notes to address your questions (Irene — flag anything I should change before we send to legal):

- Redaction/pseudonymization: Redwood supports two modes:
  * Deterministic pseudonymization (customer-scoped salt + HMAC): same input maps to same pseudonym within your tenant; reversible only if customer maintains the salt. Good for session re-association.
  * One-way irreversible tokenization (non-deterministic): recommended where reversibility is prohibited.
- KV cache & debug logs: the KV cache is a short-lived in-memory store backed to an encrypted object store when debug sampling is enabled. Access control is RBAC — only explicitly provisioned MedIntegRA debug roles can unseal the sampled logs, and all access generates immutable audit events (who/when/why). Purge is automated via lifecycle policy — we ship a cryptographic erase workflow that marks objects for immediate retention expiration then rotates keys.
- Audit evidence we can provide up front:
  1) Dataflow diagram (already attached by Irene).
  2) SOC2 control mapping doc (we will provide a scoped extract focused on retention & logging).
  3) Example DPA paragraph (Irene — legal will coordinate; I’ve pasted a short sample below for quick review).

Sample DPA paragraph (for negotiation):
"Redwood agrees to process Customer Data solely for the purpose of providing inference services. Customer may elect to enable a short-term debug cache (configured per-customer). By default, raw inputs will not be stored persistently. If Customer enables the short-term debug cache, Redwood will retain sampled debug artifacts for a configurable retention period (e.g., 72 hours) after which the artifacts are automatically and irreversibly purged. Access to debug artifacts is restricted to Customer-approved roles and is recorded in immutable audit logs"

Irene / Ben — I can join the legal/security call and walk through the KMS/key rotation guarantees and the purge workflow. Proposed times: Wed 2026-03-17 10:00-11:00 PT or Thu 2026-03-18 09:00-10:00 PT. Which works?

-Rishi
Principal Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
